profile.headline: Software Engineer at Charlie Health
profile.summary: Software Engineer building tech grounded in ethical engineering and user-driven development. Passionate about solving real-world problems for local and global communities. Always happy to connect!

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.locationName: San Diego, California, United States · Remote

positions.title: Undergraduate Research Assistant
positions.description: I worked with the humanitarian engineering department in the clean cooking sector to research biomass stoves and other clean cook stove technologies.  As part of this, I traveled to Guatemala to gain more insight into stove usage; I led the distribution of surveys in small villages near Antigua, and monitored usage and adoption during a homestay in the Lake Atitlán region.  I later began the development of a website to store and analyze data collected by a stove monitoring device, the Fuel Usage Electronic Logger (FUEL).  I wrote my undergraduate honors thesis on the development of the website, the impact of the ability to track stove usage data, and the cross cultural user experience elements that should be taken into account with a website that will be used internationally.

positions.title: Coding Instructor
positions.description: Taught 4-8 students of various levels in part-time or full-time camps, using Scratch.

volunteerExperiences.description:
I coordinated the annual banquet and silent auction for Engineers Without Borders at Oregon State.  The 2019 event had over 100 attendees and was the most profitable banquet in the club's history.  While I served in this position for two years,  the event I was planning for 2020 was canceled due to the pandemic.

This position gave me experience in large event planning, which included the development of skills in time management, leadership, delegation, technical writing, design, and organization.

I served as the Program Coordinator for the Cambodia partnership at Engineers Without Borders - OSU.  In this position, I have been responsible for leading weekly meetings, as well as managing the project as a whole.  I took on this role at the beginning of the pandemic and successfully converted our meetings and activities to the remote environment; over the last year, our membership has tripled.

In this role, not only am I responsible for running meetings, but I am also facilitating design work, coordinating with mentors, staying in contact with our partner community in Cambodia, and further assisting with grant writing to ensure funding.
